rationale_evidence.anchor: Temporal conflict ... Nexus=3.69 at t_1=2024 and Nexus=3.85 at t_2=2026. There is no contradiction if t_1\neq t_2. Temporal context must be part of conflict detection. This is one of the reasons we separated SourceTime, AcquisitionTime, ValidityTime.
rationale_evidence.statement: Requires temporal context be part of conflict detection, since two differently-timed version assertions are not contradictory — reaffirming the earlier SourceTime/AcquisitionTime/ValidityTime separation.

rationale_evidence.anchor: But dependencies can propagate revision ... A\rightarrow B where B=Infer(A). If A is retracted, B may become unsupported. Retract(A) \rightarrow Reassess(B). This is why the provenance graph is not merely an audit feature. It is part of the semantic dependency model.
rationale_evidence.statement: Argues retraction can propagate through dependency (Retract(A)→Reassess(B) when B was inferred from A), making the provenance graph part of the semantic dependency model, not merely an audit feature.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Computational viability ... For finite knowledge graphs, yes. G_K=(V,E) is finite for any finite current state. A new event affects a reachable subgraph: Reachable(e,G_K). We can recompute the affected region rather than the entire Knowledge State. ... provided the inference and semantic comparison
rationale_evidence.statement: Argues revision is computationally tractable for finite knowledge graphs by recomputing only the reachable affected subgraph Reachable(e,G_K), conditional on the inference/semantic-comparison policies themselves being computationally bounded.
